findings.text: the eight backgrounded srun arms are joined with a bare `wait`, so no arm's exit status reaches the script's own exit and a run in which every arm died still ends with ALLDONE and exit 0; gate failure is readable only from the per-arm EXIT= lines, not from the launcher. On the recorded run this is exactly what happened to the head edge-term CPU arm, whose log ends EXIT=137 with no pytest summary.

`_count` re-implements the jaxpr equation walk that scripts/prototypes/graded_residual_compile/count_graph.py:33 already owns verbatim in its CHILD string; the new copy is a narrowed variant (no list/tuple traversal, no `.eqns` fallback), so the two now disagree on any jaxpr that carries a nested scope and neither is the owner.

PANELS carries two identical (offset, end, scale) tuples, so the traced program has one distinct panel repeated twice rather than the two-panel shape the plural name and the 402-equation golden imply; the count is pinned to a narrower program than a reader is told it measures, and a later edit meant to make the panels distinct will move the golden for a reason unrelated to the Jacobian form.

the file is the change's only regression guard for the cosh Jacobian and it lives under scripts/prototypes/graded_residual_compile/, which the repository's default `pytest tests/` lane never collects, so nothing fails on a regression to sqrt(1 + sinh^2) unless a human runs this path by hand. The brief's write paths excluded tests/, so the placement is forced rather than chosen, and the gap belongs to whoever owns that lane.

the module line is appended straight after pytest's own output with no preceding newline, so the progress line and the `# module=` line fuse on one line whenever pytest ends without a summary (visible in gate/pytest-head-test_edge_term_tangents.log); the header a later reader parses for the imported module is then not on a line of its own.
